context: A mom guides her young son through polite phrases at home
purpose: Teach: 見れる/愚か/味わう/気に入ら/さよう/お断り/及ん/皆さま

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔、お客さまがいらしたら、まず「皆さま、ようこそ」って言うのよ。
lines.en: Sho, when guests arrive, first say 'welcome, everyone.'
lines.style: warm motherly tone teaching politeness gently at home

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ええー、面倒くさい。言わなかったら、愚かな子って思われるの?
lines.en: Aw, that's a hassle. If I don't say it, will they think I'm a foolish kid?
lines.style: whiny young boy pushing back with childish exaggerated worry

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 愚かじゃなくて、礼儀よ。お茶を出されたら、ゆっくり味わうの。
lines.en: Not foolish, it's manners. When tea is served, savor it slowly.
lines.style: patient correction explaining etiquette with calm maternal warmth

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: もしお菓子が気に入らなかったら、どうすればいいの?
lines.en: What if I don't like the sweets they give me?
lines.style: innocent practical question from curious child seeking guidance

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: そのときは「結構です」って丁寧にお断りするの。失礼なことしちゃダメよ。
lines.en: Then politely decline by saying 'no thank you.' Don't do anything rude.
lines.style: firm but gentle instruction reinforcing proper refusal phrasing

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: テレビでお辞儀してる人、見れるよね。話が長く及んでも、ずっと笑顔だった。
lines.en: You can see people bowing on TV, right? Even when the talk dragged on, they kept smiling.
lines.style: eager child connecting the lesson to something familiar from television

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: よく見てるのね。じゃあ最後に、お見送りのときは「さようなら」をちゃんと言いましょう。
lines.en: You really watch carefully. So lastly, at the send-off, say 'goodbye' properly.
lines.style: reassuring laugh softening the formal lesson for a small child

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: わかった!次にお客さんが来たら、ちゃんとやってみるね。
lines.en: Okay! Next time guests come, I'll try to do it properly.
lines.style: bright determined child accepting the challenge with renewed confidence
